configs.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 4 slot bays are EMPTY; psus, res are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.
configs.name: base

gaps.wanted: a corrected MX104 physical table - the module rows scramble width/depth/height (a MIC listed 15.9 cm wide when the photographed face is ~168 mm, PSU axes likewise); faces are photo-sized and marked approximate.
the AC supply face (guide Figure 9 is isometric line art only); only the photographed DC variant is modelled.
the remaining per-module wattage rows - only the 20x1GE MIC's 26 W was inside this extraction's text layer.
a DB-15 standard part - the ALARM connector is drawn as a plain cutout with its legend.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in a missing `attrs.power` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 8 bays (front 8) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

color.note: photo - medium grey face and rear

fixed-panel.note: photo - ALARM DB-15 at the left, four fixed XE SFP+ cages at centres 97.8-140.6 silkscreened 2/0/0-2/0/3, SYS OK lamp and ONLINE/OFFLINE button, EXT REF CLOCK and ToD RJ45s at 269.9/285.5, the 1PPS / 10 MHz IN-OUT SMB quad inline at 311.5-334.2, and the junos badge

lifecycle.note: announced - MX104 is EOL (TSB seen in the family tables; image-library page redirects). Per-SKU dates on the Juniper milestones page

other-faces.note: left face carries the estimated fan-tray band (side-mounted cooling per the guide); other faces rail-band estimates. Axis conventions per viewer3d.js as the siblings

populated-with.note: photo - slot 1/0 and 0/1 carry MIC-3D-20GE-SFP, slot 1/1 the MIC-3D-4CHOC3-1OC12-CE, slot 0/0 the MIC-3D-2XGE-XFP; both RE bays carry the slim MX104 RE and both PSU bays the DC supply. Defaults reproduce that configuration

power.note: guide power table - the 20x1GE MIC row (26 W) was captured; the chassis-level and remaining per-module rows fell outside this extraction's text layer and their L27 warnings stand. Max thermal and draw figures not carried rather than guessed

rear.note: photo - a plain panel with the two-hole earthing plate at the bottom centre; nothing else. The fan tray and air filter are SIDE-mounted per the guide (Figure 7/8) and appear on the left face as an estimated band

scale.note: photo - the front photograph is isotropic at 3.087 px/mm once the brackets are excluded (aspect with brackets matches the 48.7 cm over-brackets figure). Rows: fixed panel 0-44.4, MIC rows 44.4-76.5 and 76.5-108.5, PSU/RE band to 154.7. A FIRST READING put the RE rows at 13.9 mm - too thin to hold their photographed RJ45s - and the row boundary was re-derived; positions are single-pass and approximate to ~2 mm throughout

sources.note: MX104 Hardware Guide, the MX104 datasheet, and the image-library photographs mx104-front-high and mx104-rear-high. No mechanical drawing was available
